ticket.title: Telemetry log has no retention, rotation or aggregates

task.title: Telemetry log has no retention, rotation or aggregates

events.description:
FILED 2026-11-08, because no retention ticket existed - an earlier handover note in this session named GB-341 as the
retention ticket, and GB-341 is "A Verified task cannot be reopened". That was my error, recorded here so the next
reader does not go looking for a ticket that was never written.

MEASURED STATE, one session after every tool started emitting: 75 spans, 18,147 bytes, ~242 bytes per span, in a single
append-only file at `.gaugeblock/telemetry/events.jsonl`. The directory holds nothing else.

WHAT THAT IMPLIES, and the shape of the problem: at 242 bytes a span, a million spans is ~240 MB in one file that every
tool appends to and nothing ever reads back selectively. Nothing rotates it, nothing aggregates it, and nothing prunes
it. The log is the only place a run's history exists, so deleting it loses evidence - which is why this is a design
ticket rather than a cron job.

WHAT RETENTION HAS TO KEEP, which is the hard part and the reason to decide before the file is large:
  * the panel needs recent spans at full fidelity;
  * `storypole handoff` wants spans by task key (GB-309), so old spans are not automatically junk;
  * law 12 wants performance claims to persist, and a rotated-away measurement is a claim with no backing;
  * a trace that spans a rotation boundary must not be torn in half, or a duration computed across it becomes a lie.

CANDIDATE SHAPES, none chosen: size-based rotation with an aggregate sidecar (counts and duration percentiles per
binary/day, kept forever, raw spans aged out); date-partitioned files with a retention window; or keeping raw spans and
adding an index so the file is cheap to query rather than cheap to store.

The measurement above is warm and single-machine - the numbers are real, the projection is arithmetic, not a benchmark.

receipt.diff:
diff --git a/docs/CONTRACTS.md b/docs/CONTRACTS.md
index 365678c..79cb802 100644
--- a/docs/CONTRACTS.md
+++ b/docs/CONTRACTS.md
@@ -288,6 +288,15 @@ pub struct VerificationReceipt {
     /// A harness chain and a member chain are different commands, and receipts that ran different
     /// commands must not read the same (`GB-316`).
     pub chain_key: Option<String>,
+    /// Content hash of the change the receipt verified (`SP-41`). Content, not position, so a rebase or
+    /// force-push cannot orphan it the way a window of SHAs can.
+    pub diff_hash: Option<String>,
+    /// The diff itself, capped. A receipt is replayed from a ledger, so an unbounded diff would make
+    /// every read pay for one large change; truncation is marked in the text (`SP-41`).
+    pub diff: Option<String>,
+    /// Whether both ends of the recorded window still exist in the repository (`SP-41`).
+    /// `Some(false)` means the window was orphaned and the receipt is now the only record of it.
+    pub window_intact: Option<bool>,
 }
 
 /// Multi-dimensional scope coordinates for filtering across repos, crates, and AST symbols.

DELIVERED AND VERIFIED 2026-11-10 (common a992803). Retention lives in gaugeblock-workspace telemetry/retention.rs: [telemetry] max_bytes (default 8 MiB) and keep_rotations (default 3), consulted before every append, with one aggregate line written per rotation - spans, bytes, and per-binary counts with duration totals. Live proof through the real writer rather than only the unit tests: with max_bytes temporarily set to 1, one storypole list rotated the suite log (884 spans, 218008 bytes) to events.1.jsonl, left the new span in events.jsonl, and wrote an aggregate naming ten binaries. The log was merged back (885 lines) and the config restored before this receipt. Two numbers from that aggregate worth keeping: storypole 691 spans totalling 78245585 ms, outfeed 39 totalling 3307621 ms - the suite has been running storypole commands for about 21.7 hours of wall-clock span time. Provenance, and it is the same caveat as BW-33 and SP-38: the receipt below says chain default and names no repository, because this ticket scope crate workspace is not a crate any member declares, so SP-50 resolution finds no owner and the suite chain runs. The change is in common, verified by common own fmt, clippy, telemetry_retention_tests 5/5.
